description.value: A repeated-measures fMRI study examined brain activation during food visualization across early and late follicular phases and fasted and fed states in healthy young women, including associations with estradiol concentration.

spans.text: In the present study, therefore, we addressed the specific contribution of estradiol to cyclic changes in brain responses to food images and the importance of the prandial state.

description.value: Nine women completed two visits, one in the early and one in the late follicular phase; each visit included fasting and fed fMRI sessions.

spans.text: Each participant completed 2 separate visits: one in the early follicular phase (3–6 d after the onset of menstruation) and one in the late follicular phase (1 wk later).

definition.value: Main effect of prandial state (fasting/fed) in response to food visualization.

value: Brain responses to food images were significantly greater in the fed state than in the fasting state in the inferior frontal and fusiform gyri, but only during the late follicular phase.
These findings suggest that estradiol may reduce food intake by decreasing sensitivity to food cues in the ventral visual pathway under conditions of energy deprivation.

definition.value: Effect of follicular phase (early compared with late) on brain activation.

value: There was no effect of follicular phase (early compared with late) on brain activation.

value: Brain responses in the fusiform gyrus and the inferior frontal gyrus differed in accordance with prandial state during the late, high-estradiol follicular phase but not the early, low-estradiol follicular phase.
The interaction was accounted for by a significant increase in activation from fasting to the fed state during the late follicular phase.

definition.value: Positive association with the elevation in estradiol concentration from the early to the late follicular phase in the fasted state.

label.value: elevation in estradiol concentration from the early to the late follicular phase

value: Activation in the occipital cortex and cerebellum increased from the early to the late follicular phase in parallel with the rise in estradiol concentration.
These results support a preferential influence of estradiol on brain mechanisms of food-intake regulation under conditions of energy deprivation.

definition.value: Negative association with the elevation in estradiol concentration from the early to the late follicular phase in the fasted state.

value: The precuneus showed a negative correlation with the elevation in estradiol concentration from the early to the late follicular phase in the fasted state.
These results support a preferential influence of estradiol on brain mechanisms of food-intake regulation under conditions of energy deprivation.

name.value: Satiation-related changes in the late follicular phase

definition.value: Fed compared with fasting in the late follicular phase.

value: Satiation-related changes in cortical activation were enhanced during the late follicular phase.

There was a large area of activation in the left inferior frontal gyrus that also extended to the middle frontal gyrus, together with additional activation in inferior temporal and parietal areas; this satiation-related change was not seen in the early follicular phase.
